part.title: Joining a community choir

turns.text: Good morning, Westgate Community Centre, Craig speaking.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Oh, hi Craig. I'm ringing about the community choir. I'd really love to join, if you're still taking new people.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: We certainly are. I actually run the choir, so you've come to the right person. I'll just take a few details first, if that's okay. Can I have your name?
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Sure. It's Fiona Kellaway.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Is that with a C or a K at the start?
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.say: A K. It's Kellaway, K, E, L, L, A, W, A, Y.
turns.text: A K. It's Kellaway, K-E-L-L-A-W-A-Y.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Lovely, thanks. I'll make sure that goes on your name tag correctly, because we had a bit of a mix-up last week. And what's your home address, Fiona?
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.say: I'm at 27 Gilmour Road, in Yarraville. Gilmour is G, I, L, M, O, U, R.
turns.text: I'm at 27 Gilmour Road, in Yarraville. Gilmour is G-I-L-M-O-U-R.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Got it. 27 Gilmour Road. And what's the best number to reach you on?
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.say: My mobile's best, because I'm hardly ever home. It's oh four three one, seven seven two, eight five six, sorry, 865.
turns.text: My mobile's best, because I'm hardly ever home. It's 0431 772 856, sorry, 865.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: So that's oh four three one, seven seven two, eight six five. Great. Now, do you know what voice part you sing? We've got sopranos, altos, tenors and basses.
turns.text: So that's 0431 772 865. Great. Now, do you know what voice part you sing? We've got sopranos, altos, tenors and basses.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Well, I always used to put myself down as a soprano, but honestly, I struggle with the really high notes. My old choir leader said I was much more comfortable lower down.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Then we'll put you down as alto for now. We can always try your voice at the first rehearsal and move you if we need to.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: That sounds sensible.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: And have you sung in a choir before? It's not a problem if you haven't. Plenty of our members are complete beginners.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Yes, but it was a long time ago. People always assume it was at school, but our school didn't actually have a choir. I sang in the church choir in my town for about five years as a teenager.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: That's great experience. One last question for the form. How did you hear about us? We like to know which advertising actually works.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Well, my sister mentioned there was a choir somewhere around here, but she didn't know where it met. Then I saw a poster on the noticeboard at the library, and it had your number on it.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Good to know. We only put those up last month, so I'm glad someone's reading them.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: So when do you rehearse?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: It used to be Tuesday nights, but quite a few members had trouble getting here then. So since February we've moved to Thursday evenings. We start at seven and finish at nine, in the main hall.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Right. That's fine for me. Do I need to bring anything along?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Just a pencil, so you can mark your music. We hand out a folder with all the songs, so you don't need to buy anything. Oh, and bring a water bottle. The hall gets very warm, and singing for two hours is thirsty work.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: I can imagine. And what are the fees?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: We charge by the term. It was eighty dollars last year, but the cost of hiring the hall went up, so it's now ninety dollars a term. That covers your sheet music as well.
turns.text: We charge by the term. It was $80 last year, but the cost of hiring the hall went up, so it's now $90 a term. That covers your sheet music as well.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: That's reasonable. Is there a discount for students? My daughter might want to come too.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: Yes, students pay sixty dollars a term, so she'd save a bit.
turns.text: Yes, students pay $60 a term, so she'd save a bit.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Good. And can I pay by card when I come in?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Ah, normally yes, but the card machine at the front desk is broken at the moment, and we're still waiting on a new one. So for now it's cash at the desk, or you can pay online through our website.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: No worries. I'll just bring it with me on the night.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Now, we've got two concerts coming up. The second one's our Christmas concert in December, but the first is the winter concert on the twenty-first of June.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Is that held here at the centre?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: We did it here last year, but the hall was far too small for all the families. So this year it's going to be at the town hall in Footscray. There's much more room.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Oh, that'll be nice. And is there a uniform for the concerts?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Nothing fancy. Black trousers or a black skirt. A few people asked about wearing blue on top, but we decided a white top looks better under the lights. And we'll give you a red scarf on the night.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Easy enough. I've got all of that already. So I just turn up next Thursday?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: That's right. Come about ten minutes early and I'll introduce you to the other altos.
turns.speaker: organiser

turns.text: Perfect. Thanks so much, Craig. See you then.
turns.speaker: caller
